lesson.content:
## What it is
The network layer is responsible for delivering packets from the source host to the destination host, possibly across many networks. It handles logical addressing, routing, forwarding, packetizing, and congestion control. [p. 1]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine you're sending a letter to a friend who lives in a different city. The network layer is like the postal service, ensuring your letter reaches your friend's mailbox, even if it has to pass through different post offices and roads. [p. 1]

## How it works
1. The network layer assigns a logical address (IP address) to each host, which is used to identify the destination host. [p. 1]
2. It then routes the packets through routers, which store and forward the packets until they reach the destination. [p. 1]
3. The network layer also manages congestion control to prevent network performance from dropping due to too many packets. [p. 1]

## Key terms
- **Logical addressing**: A 32-bit (IPv4) address given by the network, used by the network layer to reach hosts on any network. [p. 1]
- **Physical addressing**: A 48-bit address burned into the network card, used inside one network by the data link layer. [p. 1]

## Example
A host sends a packet to the nearest router. The router stores the whole packet until it has arrived completely and its checksum is verified, then forwards it to the next router, until it reaches the destination. [p. 1]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 1]

## Exam tip
Describe the process of packet delivery from source to destination, including routing and congestion control. [p. 1]
